newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: EVANS SAYS COLSTON CALL HYPOCRITICAL
Deputy Opposition leader Gareth Evans says he has no problem with a call for all Senators to table their travel allowance details in the Upper House.
The call comes from Independent Senator Mal Colston who's currently being investigated for alleged travel rorts.
Senator Evans says he'd be happy to reveal details if it would help restore confidence in the integrity of parliamentarians.
But he says it's hypocritical that Senator Colston made the call, when last year he approached the Privacy Commissioner, when called on to reveal details of his use of parliamentary allowances.
FOURTH DEATH UNDER NT VOLUNTARY EUTHANASIA LAW
A 70-year-old Sydney woman, who'd been suffering from cancer, has become the fourth person to use the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law.
The woman died on the weekend using a machine-assisted lethal injection, and was aided by Darwin doctor Phillip Nitschke.
CLONCURRY DECLARED A DISASTER AREA
The flood-affected town of Cloncurry in Queensland's north west has been declared a disaster area.
Emergency Services Minister Mick Vievers says the disaster declaration will enable the residents, businesss and farmers to receive flood relief from state and federal governments.
Meanwhile, emergency workers in Cloncurry are on full alert as the swollen Cloncurry River continues to rise.
Police are recommending people move from low lying homes for the second time in three days.
BEAZLEY ON LEGAL AID FUNDING
The Federal Opposition says the Government won't fix the legal aid crisis by shifting funds within the Attorney-General's Department.
Kim Beazley says the Attorney-General has consistently said no more money will be provided for legal aid, but several States have indicated they've been offered increased Commonweath funding.
Mr Beazley says if that's to be funded from cuts to the Department, law and order as a whole will be compromised, including the Federal Police and the National Crime Authority.
He says providing additional resources is the only way the problem can be dealt with.
TRANSPORT CO-ORDINATING AUTHORITY FOR OLYMPICS
As expected the New South Wales Government has announced an olympic roads and transport authority to co-ordinate transport services for the olympics.
Olympics Minister Michael Knight will receive reports from the authority which will integrate all government and private sector transport services with olympic requirements.
Premier Bob Carr says the need for a single olympics roads and transport organisation was one of the key lessons from the Atlanta games.
SUPERLEAGUE CONCERNS OVER WIRING OF REFS
Super League officials are meeting in Sydney at the moment to discuss concerns over the wiring of referees.
For last week's opening round the referees were wired for sound enabling televison viewers to hear their remarks, but it appears the innovation was not well received by the viewers.
Ratings figures indicate many turned the telecast off. - - - -
CASINO INCOMES SHOW 36 PERCENT INCREASE
Australia's 14 casinos had a gross income of more than 2.2 billion dollars for the 95-96 financial year.
Figures released today by the Australian Bureau of Statistics says that's a 36 percent increase over the previoous year.
Takings from gambling accounted for 1.8 billion dollars, or 84 percent of grossincome.
The Bureau of Statistics says the casino industry now employs nearly 18 and a half thousand people, a 17 percent increase over 12 months.
